items.prompt:
A cost-benefit comparison weighs
A) benefits against costs
B) only colors
C) only names
D) only the date

steps: It weighs good points against costs.

items.prompt:
Coal is a ____ resource.
A) non-renewable
B) renewable
C) living
D) imaginary

Solar energy is
A) renewable
B) non-renewable
C) a fossil fuel
D) a mineral

Coal provides lots of energy but has the cost of
A) heavy air pollution
B) no pollution
C) running out of sunlight
D) nothing

A cheaper mining plan that harms a river trades
A) money for the environment
B) the environment for nothing
C) energy for jobs
D) nothing at all

steps: It trades money against the environment.

items.prompt:
Considering whether a resource is renewable matters because non-renewable resources
A) run out, a long-term cost
B) last forever
C) have no cost
D) make no pollution
items.answer: A) run out, a long-term cost

steps: Running out is a long-term cost.

items.prompt:
A renewable source that costs more now but lasts and pollutes less often has
A) the better long-term cost-benefit
B) no benefits
C) the worst cost-benefit
D) no costs at all

steps: Lasting, cleaner energy pays off long term.

items.prompt:
The best reason to compare competing resource solutions is to
A) choose the one with the best balance of benefits and costs
B) pick the newest
C) pick randomly
D) avoid all resources
items.answer: A) choose the one with the best balance of benefits and costs
